The '''2020–21 Primeira Liga''' (also known as '''Liga NOS''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 87th season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. The season started later than usual, on 18 September 2020, due to the [[2019–20 Primeira Liga#Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic|delayed end of the previous season caused by the COVID-19 pandemic]], and it concluded on 19 May 2021.

This was the fourth Primeira Liga season to use [[Video assistant referee|video assistant referee (VAR)]]. As was the case at the end of the previous season, there were [[Behind closed doors (sport)|limited or no attendance]] in the stadiums besides each team's staff and personnel.

[[FC Porto|Porto]] were the defending champions. [[Clube Desportivo Nacional|Nacional]] and [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] were promoted from the second-tier [[2019–20 LigaPro]] by decision of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional]], after the suspension of the 2019–20 LigaPro due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]. They replaced [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]] and [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]], who were relegated to the [[2020–21 Campeonato de Portugal]].

On 11 May 2021, [[Sporting CP]] secured a 19th title after a 1–0 home win against [[Boavista F.C.|Boavista]], their first title since the [[2001–02 Primeira Liga|2001–02 season]]. It was also the first title since that season not being won by either [[SL Benfica|Benfica]] or [[FC Porto|Porto]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2021/05/12/football/sporting-lisbon-title-win-covid-19-cmd-spt-intl/index.html|title=Sporting Lisbon's bittersweet title win after 19 years of hurt|last=Cotovio|first=Vasco|date=12 May 2021|publisher=CNN|access-date=7 April 2022}}</ref>

Since Portugal ascended from seventh to sixth place in the [[UEFA coefficient#League coefficient|UEFA association coefficient rankings]] at the end of 2019–20 season, the three best-ranked teams could qualify for the [[UEFA Champions League]] (the champions and runners-up entered directly into the group stage, and the third placed team entered the third qualifying round). The fourth and fifth-placed teams would qualified respectively to the [[UEFA Europa Conference League]] play-off and third qualifying rounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-23 |title=UEFA Coefficient Rankings: Portugal overtake Russia |url=https://proxima-jornada.com/2019/10/23/uefa-coefficient-rankings-portugal-overtake-russia/ |access-date=2023-06-05 |website=PRÓXIMA JORNADA |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic==
Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]], since March 2020, in contrast with various [[UEFA|European leagues]], the Primeira Liga began playing matches [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]]. On 13 September, [[Sporting CP|Sporting]] confirmed that three players had tested positive for [[coronavirus]], leading their pre-season match against [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] to be cancelled due to the orders of the Portuguese [[Ministry of Health (Portugal)|Ministry of Health]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.noticiasaominuto.com/desporto/1583027/casos-de-covid-19-obrigam-sporting-a-cancelar-jogo-com-o-napoli|title = Casos de Covid-19 obrigam Sporting a cancelar jogo com o Napoli|date = 13 September 2020}}</ref> The following day, Sporting confirmed that four players and a member of their staff had tested positive for coronavirus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://expresso.pt/tribuna|title=Tribuna|website=Expresso}}</ref> Meanwhile, [[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]] confirmed that fifteen players had tested positive for coronavirus, leading also their pre-season match against [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]] to be cancelled.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.publico.pt/2020/09/13/desporto/noticia/gil-vicente-15-casos-covid19-1931458|title=Gil Vicente com 15 casos de covid-19 no plantel. Quarentena obrigatória decretada|first=Miguel|last=Dantas|website=PÚBLICO}}</ref> Three days later, Sporting confirmed that their manager [[Ruben Amorim]] and another player tested positive for coronavirus, with both going into self-isolation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-nos/sporting/amp/noticia-record-ruben-amorim-testa-positivo-a-covid-19|title = Notícia Record: Rúben Amorim testa positivo à Covid-19 - Sporting - Jornal Record}}</ref> On 17 September, it was announced that the Gil Vicente and Sporting fixture on matchday 1 would be postponed, following direct orders from the Portuguese Ministry of Health, after it was confirmed that Gil Vicente had four more positive cases of coronavirus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://observador.pt/2020/09/17/sporting-gil-vicente-tera-sido-adiado-leoes-tem-10-infetados-equipa-de-barcelos-tem-15-casos-decisao-foi-tomada-pela-ars-norte/amp/|title=Sporting-Gil Vicente foi adiado: leões têm 10 infetados, equipa de Barcelos tem 19 casos. Decisão foi tomada pela ARS Norte – Observador|website=observador.pt}}</ref>
 
On 3 October, [[C.D. Santa Clara|Santa Clara]] faced [[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]] on matchday 3 at the [[Estádio de São Miguel (Ponta Delgada)|Estádio de São Miguel]], in [[Ponta Delgada]], [[Azores]], in a match, which was the first one to allow spectators in Portugal, with the stadium being limited to 10% of its capacity (1,000 spectators).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zap.aeiou.pt/publico-voltou-estadios-acores-350948|title = Balanço "extremamente positivo". Público voltou aos estádios nos Açores|date = 4 October 2020}}</ref> Ten days later, it was announced that [[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]]'s manager [[Pepa (footballer)|Pepa]] had tested positive for [[COVID-19]], leading him and his staff being placed in quarantine as a preventive measure, forcing him to miss Paços de Ferreira's match against Santa Clara on October 18 at matchday 4.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-bwin/p--ferreira/detalhe/pepa-infetado-com-covid-19|title=Pepa infetado com Covid-19|website=www.record.pt}}</ref>

On matchday 5, played between 23 and 26 October, there were three matches in which spectatores were allowed: [[C.D. Tondela|Tondela]] against [[Portimonense S.C.|Portimonense]] at [[Estádio João Cardoso]], Santa Clara against Sporting at the Estádio de São Miguel (with spectators being allowed for the second consecutive match) and [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] against [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]] at [[Estádio Algarve]], where Farense played their first three home matches, instead of their regular home stadium [[Estádio de São Luís]], due to a turf change.
Like the match against Gil Vicente, Santa Clara match was played with the stadium capacity limited to 10%,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://desporto.sapo.pt/futebol/primeira-liga/artigos/covid-19-confirmada-a-presenca-de-publico-no-santa-clara-sporting|title=Covid-19: Confirmada a presença de público no Santa Clara–Sporting|website=SAPO Desporto}}</ref> as the other two matches were limited to 15% (approximately 750 and 4,500 spectators in Estádio João Cardoso and Estádio Algarve, respectively).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/liga/adeptos/tondela-portimonense-e-farense-rio-ave-vao-ter-publico|title = Tondela-Portimonense e Farense-Rio Ave vão ter público}}</ref>

Santa Clara announced on February 20 that spectators will be allowed in Estádio de São Miguel, for the third time this season, in the match against Paços de Ferreira on matchday 21, played one week later on 27 February. This time, one third of the stadium's maximum capacity was allowed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/noticias/nota-a-imprensa-sobre-regresso-do-publico-no-santa-clara-fc-p-ferreira?bck=L3B0L2hvbWVwYWdlLw|title = Nota à Imprensa sobre regresso do público no Santa Clara - FC P. Ferreira}}</ref>

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league – the top sixteen teams from [[2019–20 Primeira Liga|the previous season]] and two teams promoted from the [[2019–20 LigaPro|LigaPro]]. [[Clube Desportivo Nacional|Nacional]] and [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] were promoted on 5 May 2020 by decision of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional]], after the suspension of the [[2019–20 LigaPro]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]. This decision was made based on [[UEFA]]'s recommendations, focusing on sporting merit, as these teams were in first and second place of the LigaPro, respectively, at the time of cancellation.<ref>{{cite web|date=5 May 2020|url=https://www.ligaportugal.pt/pt/epocas/20192020/noticias/institucional/direcao-da-liga-portugal-em-reuniao-extraordinaria/|title=Direção da Liga Portugal em reunião extraordinária|trans-title=LPFP board extraordinary meeting|language=pt|website=[[Liga Portuguesa de Futebol Profissional|LPFP]]|access-date=6 May 2020}}</ref>

Nacional came back to the top division one season after being relegated, while Farense secured their return after an 18-year absence. They replaced [[C.D. Aves|Desportivo das Aves]] and [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]], who were relegated after three and sixteen seasons in the top flight, respectively.

==Awards==
===Monthly awards===
For the 2020–21 season, there were seven monthly awards in the Primeira Liga: best player, goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, forward, manager and goal of the month.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Best of September/October 2020-21: Pedro Gonçalves and Gonçalo Ramos are the highlights of the month|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/en/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/premios/setembrooutubro/melhores-de-setembrooutubro-2020-21-pedro-goncalves-e-goncalo-ramos-em-destaque/|access-date=2021-03-13|website=Liga Portugal|archive-date=26 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026171826/https://www.ligaportugal.pt/en/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/premios/setembrooutubro/melhores-de-setembrooutubro-2020-21-pedro-goncalves-e-goncalo-ramos-em-destaque/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Best of December 2020-21: Sérgio Oliveira and Crespo are the highlights of the month|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/en/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/premios/dezembro/melhores-de-dezembro-2020-21-sergio-oliveira-e-crespo-em-destaque/|access-date=2021-03-13|website=Liga Portugal|archive-date=9 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509201131/https://www.ligaportugal.pt/en/epocas/20202021/noticias/geral/premios/dezembro/melhores-de-dezembro-2020-21-sergio-oliveira-e-crespo-em-destaque/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
